reasons: Rule-accurate classification: Delaware governing law (Section 13.6.1) is expressly within the playbook fallback, and the finding correctly declines to redline it up to New York — no over-flagging.

The forum uncertainty is real and well-evidenced: Section 13.7.1 makes arbitration the mandatory end-point, Section 13.7.3 defers wholly to Schedule 13.7.3, and the Schedule text is redacted at p0701, so the seat/rules cannot be verified against the walk-away trigger (arbitration seated abroad).

Consistent with the needs_review posture, no redline or counterparty comment is proposed; the redline output is byte-identical to the original paragraphs and the deterministic governing-law check passes, so nothing invalid or directionally wrong is being introduced.

Rationale is factually supported by the cited text (IP validity/enforceability carve-out in 13.7.2, interim relief preserved in 13.7.5, caption/submission-to-jurisdiction gap in 13.6.2 noted but not double-flagged) and gives an actionable next step: obtain Schedule 13.7.3 and, if the seat is outside the accepted list, redline the seat only while leaving Delaware law intact.
